items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron for Science: open model, ~50k-question chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for research agents
items.summary: NVIDIA announced Nemotron for Science at SC26: open models, datasets, tools and post-training recipes for building science agents. A companion walkthrough post-trains Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with NeMo Gym and NeMo RL; outside posts describe a LitmusBench v0.2 chemistry set of nearly 50,000 questions.

reception.summary: Most replies were off-topic calls to bring back Jensen Huang; the few on-topic ones praised the open chemistry data and the plan-simulate-check loop. Nobody reported trying it.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-Sigma: open-weight 3B and 8B continuous diffusion language models with few-step distills
items.summary: NVIDIA published 3B and 8B diffusion language models as base, instruct, few-step distilled (2, 4, 8, 16 steps) and self-speculative variants. The poster notes they need an NVIDIA GPU with custom code, no GGUF and nothing for Macs yet, and quality drops below about 16 steps, so the 2- and 4-step distills are the ones to try locally.

items.title: InferenceBench update: Gemini 4 Carbon ranks #3 and Gemini 4 Hydrogen #8
items.summary: The InferenceBench author reports new standings with Gemini 4 Carbon third and Gemini 4 Hydrogen eighth. The post shows a leaderboard image and gives no method or link in the text.
